Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Wix, Squarespace, Magento and custom sites. We tailor the fix notes to what your platform allows.

desc:
An ecommerce SEO audit with a fix list shows you exactly what holds your online store back in search. Ecom Swift LLC crawls your site, reviews it the way a search engine does, and hands you a ranked list of problems in plain English.

## What is an ecommerce SEO audit?

An ecommerce SEO audit is a structured review of your store that finds the technical, content and linking problems limiting how well your pages appear in search. It ends with a written report, not a vague opinion. Each finding says what is wrong, where it happens, why it matters and how to fix it.

Online stores need this more than most sites. They have hundreds or thousands of near-identical pages, filters that create extra addresses, and product text that often arrives straight from a supplier. Problems build up quietly, and the store owner rarely sees them from the admin screen.

## Why a store audit is worth doing before any other SEO work

Spending on content, ads or link building while the foundation is cracked wastes effort. If search engines cannot reach a collection page, or see ten copies of the same product, new text on top of it changes little. An audit tells you which problems are real and which are noise, so you fix the expensive ones first.

## How an SEO audit affects traffic and sales

Search visits come from pages that search engines can find, understand and trust. An audit improves the first two directly. When broken links, duplicate pages and missing titles are repaired, crawlers spend their time on the pages that earn money. When thin product text and weak internal links are strengthened, those pages give search engines more to work with.

The effect on revenue is indirect but real: more of your products and collections become eligible to appear for relevant searches, and the visitors who arrive land on pages that work. What a store gains depends on its competition, its history and how quickly the fixes are made, so we describe the work and never promise a position.

## What a thorough store audit covers

- Crawl of your pages, listing errors, redirects and blocked addresses.
- Page titles, headings and meta descriptions that are missing, duplicated or too long.
- Duplicate and near-duplicate pages caused by variants, filters and tags.
- Thin product and collection text that gives search engines little to read.
- Broken internal and outgoing links.
- Indexing and sitemap health, including pages that should be listed but are not.
- Template speed problems that slow product and collection pages.
- Internal links, and whether your best pages receive enough of them.
- A priority order, so the biggest problems come first.

## How we run your audit

First we set up a crawl of your store and read the data your platform and Search Console already hold. Then we review the results by hand, because a tool alone flags many harmless items and misses the ones that matter in context.

The report groups findings by impact and effort, with a short note on how to fix each one. The Basic package focuses on the most important issues. The Standard package widens the crawl and adds duplicate, indexing and sitemap findings, plus a manual look at your top product pages. The Premium package adds a comparison with competing stores, an internal link review and a three month action plan, with a call to talk it through.

You can take the list to your own developer, or order the fixes from us as separate work. An optional backlink snapshot and a walkthrough call are available as add-ons.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share the pages and products you care about most, so the review weighs them properly.
- Tell us about recent changes, such as a new theme or a platform move.
- Fix the high-impact items first before touching small ones.
- Re-check the store after changes are made.
- Keep a copy of the report for future developers.

**Avoid:**
- Treating every warning from a tool as equally urgent.
- Deleting pages without setting up a redirect to a close match.
- Running an audit in the middle of a redesign, when the pages are about to change.
- Expecting the report alone to change your traffic. The fixes do that.

## Who this audit is for

A store owner whose traffic has flattened and who does not know why will find the report useful. So will a seller who recently changed themes or apps and wants to check nothing broke. A business that has paid for SEO before and cannot tell what was done will gain a clear independent picture.

## What we need from you

Send us your store address and tell us what you sell, who your main competitors are, and which pages matter most. If you have Search Console and analytics, add us as a user so we can read the data. We never need your password, and we do not need the ability to edit anything for an audit. Access, where needed, is given through a collaborator, staff or viewer account in your own tools.
